scenario: Validate the documented software-engineering lifecycle route and its contracts, optional-stage approvals, verifier separation, fixed-point continuity, rollback ownership, and maintenance feedback edge.
prompt: validate the lifecycle graph from requirements through maintenance and corrective requirements; emit a typed acyclic route with artifact contracts, verifier edges, fixed-point digests, operational ownership, rollback evidence, and fail-closed dispositions.
context: requirements-engineering, architecture-evaluation, codebase-design, domain-modeling, to-tickets, implement, testing, skill-quality-gate, review-pr, release-management, deployment, observability, sre, and software-maintenance-evolution are canonical skills
maintenance feedback starts a new requirements revision rather than creating an in-run cycle
optional stages require not-applicable evidence and exact approval
the producer cannot be its own verifier
missing digests, owners, rollback evidence, or authoritative recovery state fail closed

instructionFollowing.criterion: The route preserves typed contracts and fixed-point continuity.
Verifier separation and optional approvals are fail-closed.
Maintenance feedback starts a new revision without an in-run cycle.

levels.4: new run edge and ownership are explicit

goalCompletion.criterion: Lifecycle graph contains nodes, edges, contracts, owners, and verifiers.

levels.4: all required graph fields are present
digest, rollback, authority, and owner gaps are blocked

goalCompletion.criterion: The graph is acyclic within a fixed run.

check.criterion: Required artifact, owner, digest, verifier, and rollback gaps fail closed

levels.pass: each missing contract is blocked or audit-incomplete
levels.fail: the route assumes completion or silently skips the stage

check.criterion: Maintenance feeds a new corrective requirements revision without violating acyclicity

levels.pass: feedback is a new run/revision edge
levels.fail: maintenance mutates the prior baseline or creates an in-run cycle
